source: RFC 0007 §7.4, §7.5 (DR2-E-1, DR2-E-3, RC review round 2 areas E to H; design set by the maintainer's coordinator, 2026-11-24)
statement: What a grant analysis could not prove contained is recorded bounded whatever the change's shape: the unknown fragments of one statement of a policy, for one reason, are one escalation, whose subject names the statement, the reason, how many fragments it stands for and the SHA-256 of them all, and whose detail names the first three, each clipped. At most 200 statements are an escalation each; the fragments of the statements past them are one TOO_LARGE escalation, counted and digested the same way. Grouping changes neither whether a change needs an approval (it does exactly when a fragment is not known contained) nor what an approval covers: an approval covers the subjects it was shown, so a fragment more, fewer or another in a group, or in the rest, is a subject it does not cover, and the change needs an approval again. What the bound leaves out is not analysed, never informational and never lifted by the role class (CTL-79). contract/control/escalations.json states the bound.
guards: control:UnknownEscalationsTest#the unknown fragments of one statement are one escalation, counted, naming the first few - CTL-88
control:UnknownEscalationsTest#each statement and each reason is an escalation of its own - CTL-88
control:UnknownEscalationsTest#past the group bound the rest is one TOO_LARGE escalation, which needs an approval - CTL-88
control:UnknownEscalationsTest#a change needs an approval exactly when it did before the grouping - CTL-88
control:UnknownEscalationsTest#a fragment more, fewer or another is a subject an approval of the others does not cover - CTL-88
control:UnknownEscalationsTest#what the escalations hold is bounded whatever the fragments - CTL-88
control:GroupedEscalationApprovalTest#an approval of a statement's fragments covers them, and not one more of them
control:EscalationBoundsTest#a proposal of tens of thousands of unproven fragments records a bounded list - CTL-88
control:ClientContractTest#a change's escalations follow the bounds of their contract file - CTL-88
